title: Holistic regional autoscale and data-residency controls for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a cohesive policy and control plane for regional and multi-zone Dedicated fleets that enforces throughput guarantees, autoscaling rules, and hard data-residency constraints while providing deterministic failover behavior. This ticket covers the control-plane policy model, runtime orchestrator changes for placement and spillover, API surface for tenant config, and the rollout/test plan. The design must: 1) expose per-tenant throughput reservations and burst gates, 2) allow soft and hard zone/region affinity with controllable spillover policies, 3) guarantee that traffic routed to a region does not store or process customer payload outside allowed geographies except via explicit emergency override, and 4) provide measurable SLOs for latency and throughput under scale events.
background_and_rationale: Customers purchasing Dedicated capacity expect predictable throughput, isolation, and data residency controls. Current runtime supports per-pool reservations and simple zone affinity but lacks a unified policy layer that composes reservations, autoscale triggers, and residency constraints. Incidents during regional maintenance revealed unpredictable spillover that violated residency guarantees for a handful of tenants. This work prevents reoccurrence and enables enterprise sales motions for regulated customers.
acceptance_criteria: API: New tenant config accepts throughput_reservation (tokens/s), min_instances, max_instances, zone_affinity (prefer|require|avoid), region_residency (allowlist of regions), and spillover_policy (block|soft|emergency)
Orchestrator: Placement decisions respect region_residency strictly when policy is 'require' and return a 409 or queue the request instead of routing out-of-region
Autoscaler: Implements two trigger classes: demand-driven (qps/token usage) and health-driven (node failure), honoring tenant min/max and providing a predictable warmup window
Failover: On AZ drain, requests are routed to same-region zones when possible; cross-region spillover only occurs when spillover_policy=soft and SLA-based countdown has elapsed
Metrics: Expose tenant-level metrics: reserved_throughput_used, effective_instances, cross_region_routed_percent, residency_violations_count
Tests: End-to-end integration tests simulate zone drain, region outage, and scaling to max; no residency_violations_count for tenants with region_residency=require
Docs: Console UI surfaces the new fields and warns on misconfigurations; API docs and migration guide provided
technical_notes: Control-plane: add a Policy object that composes Reservation, Affinity, Residency, Spillover. Store as tenant-scoped immutable revisions for safe rollback.

Orchestrator changes: extend planner to evaluate candidate placements by scoring: residency_score (infinite penalty for violations when 'require'), throughput_headroom_score, warm_instance_penalty to prefer prewarmed nodes.

Autoscaling algorithm: decouple reactive scale-up from proactive prewarm. Prewarm uses predictive short-term forecast for tenants above threshold and maintains a per-tenant warmup_budget to meet throughput SLOs.
KV cache implications: ensure cache pinning is region-aware; when routing across zones within a region prefer nodes with hot KV cache to avoid cold-start latency penalties.

Emergency override: provide auditable operator action 'evacuate-residency' that can be used only with SSO 2FA and logs the justification; overrides count against 'residency_violation' metric for post-mortem.

Data plane: enforce egress host filtering and region-tagged logging to make residency verification possible from audit logs. Integrate with KMS key scoping so that keys bound to a region are only used on nodes with matching region tag.
Backward compatibility: default tenant policy should behave as today (zone affine preferred, soft spillover allowed). Migration job will present tenants with explicit policy opt-in in Console.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal canary): Deploy control-plane changes to staging; migrate internal test tenants; validate metrics and operator overrides
Phase 1 (opt-in tenants): Provide API + Console controls; invite 3 pilot customers from existing Dedicated pool with varied residency needs
Phase 2 (wider rollout): Gate new policy as opt-in default for new Dedicated enrollments; run a 2-week soak in production in a limited region

Phase 3 (enforcement): Make 'require' residency policy available for purchase and enforce routing restrictions by default; disable emergency auto-spillover for 'require' unless operator override applied
Rollback plan: revert control-plane policy pointer to previous revision and drain newly placed prewarm instances; have a manual operator runbook for live rollback
test_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation logic and planner scoring functions
Integration test harness simulating kube/node failures, AZ-level network partition, and regional blackout to validate spillover_policy behavior
Chaos experiments: random AZ drains under load for opt-in tenants to verify throughput SLOs and no residency violation when 'require'
Load tests to prove prewarm reduces p95 latency during scale events by target delta (expected p95 improvement >= 150ms)
Security review checklist for emergency override and KMS scoping
monitoring_and_slo: Expose tenant SLOs: throughput_guarantee (tokens/s), p95_latency, availability_percent
Alerting: residency_violation > 0 triggers pager for oncall-security and oncall-runtime
Dashboards: tenant-level dedicated capacity view showing shard-to-zone mapping, warm_instances, and cross_region_routed_percent
SLA breach policy: if throughput_guarantee unmet for 5m after autoscale attempts, escalate and trigger compensating credits flow
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-constraining placements may reduce utilization. Mitigation: expose economic tradeoff in Console and allow soft spillover with cost-awareness
Risk: Predictive prewarm may waste capacity. Mitigation: limit prewarm budget per tenant and decay allocations for low-util tenants
Risk: Operator overrides could lead to compliance incidents. Mitigation: require 2FA, log and surface reasons, plus automated post-incident audits
Risk: Complex planner scoring could increase scheduling latency. Mitigation: precompute candidate pools and cache scoring for common tenant profiles
